findings.claim: the Temple of Apollo had a colonnaded portico of 48 Doric columns
findings.truth: The Temple of Apollo itself was a peripteral temple with 48 Ionic columns; its wider sacred enclosure also had Ionic columns before later alteration.
findings.evidence: Temple of Apollo (Pompeii), fetched 2026-09-05, architecture section; Zanker, Pompeii: Public and Private Life, cited there.

findings.claim: There was no running water above the ground floor in insulae, and the practice material treats lack of indoor sanitation above ground level as a known condition.
findings.truth: Water and sanitation varied by building. Strabo reports running water and sanitation in insulae, and evidence from larger Ostian insulae indicates upper floors could have kitchens, latrines and piped water. Public fountains and shared facilities were also used.
findings.evidence: Insula (building), fetched 2026-09-05, construction and Ostia sections; Ostia Antica, fetched 2026-09-05, residential-buildings section.

findings.claim: The AD 79 eruption began in the late morning and lasted over eighteen hours.
findings.truth: The eruption began in the early afternoon. Its initial pumice-fall phase lasted about eighteen hours, but the eruption as a whole lasted for around two days.
findings.evidence: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, fetched 2026-09-05, nature-of-the-eruption section; Pompeii, fetched 2026-09-05, eruption section.

findings.claim: Pliny the Elder died of asphyxiation on the beach at Stabiae.
findings.truth: Pliny the Elder died at Stabiae, but the cause cannot be established from the evidence. His nephew suggested poisonous gas, while later discussion also proposes a stroke, heart attack or asthma attack.
findings.evidence: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, fetched 2026-09-05, Pliny the Elder section; it summarises Pliny's account and the competing explanations.

findings.claim: The AD 62 earthquake had disrupted normal life for seventeen years, so many Pompeian buildings were still under repair at the eruption.
findings.truth: Keep the AD 62 earthquake, but choose between two accounts: retain only a cautious point that individual repairs and rebuilding occurred, or revise the wider evaluation. Recent scholarship summarised in the fetched source says the longstanding claim of widespread unfinished repairs is doubtful; much rebuilding and new public construction occurred, and Pompeii was still flourishing. This change affects the content, key fact, conclusion, exam tip, practice answer and flashcard.
findings.evidence: Pompeii, fetched 2026-09-05, AD 62-79 section, citing current archaeological research.
findings.ruling: Cautious account: earthquake kept as a limitation; the settled 'seventeen years of disruption, many buildings under repair' claim softened in content, takeaway and flashcard; exam tip and mark scheme only say 'disrupted', left.

findings.claim: “The fruit sellers, together with Helvius Vestalis, urge you to elect Marcus Holconius Priscus as duumvir for the administration of justice.”
findings.truth: This English wording is presented as a direct inscription quotation, but it could not be verified against a fetched primary text or accessible edition. Treat it as a paraphrase or supply a verifiable source before retaining quotation marks.
findings.evidence: The lesson attributes the rendering to Cooley and Cooley, Pompeii: A Sourcebook; no fetchable primary text or accessible edition was available in this check.

summary: Five lessons were checked against OCR J199 and fetched historical sources. Four verified factual findings have surgical edits; the earthquake interpretation requires a unit-wide editorial decision.
